# INSIGHTS — summarized, verified findings (accumulate across the whole run)

The JOURNAL is your per-iteration diary; THIS file is the distilled, VERIFIED takeaway a future iteration should read instead of re-reading the whole journal or old sessions/traces. Update it whenever you have a genuinely NEW, confirmed finding (an accepted/rejected RESULT counts as confirmation; a guess does not) — not every iteration needs a new entry. Structure each addition as:

    ## <task or mechanism name>
    - What worked (confirmed by a RESULT, cite the candidate id):
    - What didn't (confirmed by a RESULT, cite the candidate id):
    - Promising but not yet tried:

## Reply-channel form (```python fence vs tool-call wrapper)
- What worked (confirmed by RESULT, `r1_contract`): a worked fenced example plus naming the exact wrapper tokens the model emits (`<|tool_call>`, `call:python_interpreter`, `<function_calls>`) as a *symptom* with its consequence ("nothing runs; after three such replies the task is abandoned with no output file"). 13-1 fixed in both screen and full val. 5/40 val tasks were failing this way with no output file at all — the cheapest cluster in the run.
- What didn't: n/a.
- Promising but not yet tried: nothing — treat this cluster as closed unless traces show it return.

## Grader contract (sheet identity + cell types)
- What worked (confirmed by RESULT, `r1_contract`): forbidding `DataFrame.to_excel`/`pd.ExcelWriter` for output_path **with the reasons stated**, paired with a worked `openpyxl.load_workbook(IN) → ws[a1] = v → wb.save(OUT)` recipe, and a "write values in their NATIVE Python type" rule. 44913 went 0→1 (it had every value correct and scored 0 on `worksheet not found`). Verified in source: `evaluation.py:cell_level_compare` returns `(False, "worksheet not found")` when the sheet name is absent, and `compare_cell_value` rejects `type(v1) != type(v2)`.
- What didn't: n/a.
- Promising but not yet tried: nothing further needed here.

## Preview coordinates
- What worked (confirmed by RESULT, `r1_contract`): "preview row i is Excel row i+2, pandas column j is Excel column j+1" — the adapter's `_spreadsheet_preview` itself annotates the extent as `rows 1-{nrows+1}` because pandas consumes row 1 as the header. Do not remove this.
- Promising but not yet tried: the preview's stated `data extent` can UNDERSTATE the workbook's own reference range (41978's extent said rows 1-185 while its own formulas span `$G$14:$G$9696`). Unresolved whether a rule about that helps or hurts.

## Verification that verifies nothing
- What worked (confirmed by RESULT, `r1_contract`): a copyable CHECK recipe that re-opens the SAVED file, addresses cells by literal A1 names (never by the write indices), prints sheetnames, and prints the EMPTY set and the CHANGED set; plus an explicit FINISH condition ("reply with no code block once CHECK is all-clear") and "never re-send an identical block" — without the latter, traces showed the same block re-sent 20–26 times.
- What didn't (confirmed by RESULT, `r1_contract`): the EMPTY/CHANGED recipe is a *presence and blast-radius* check, NOT a correctness check. 41978 printed `EMPTY: 0 []` / `CHANGED: 10 [...]` — exactly the expected shape — on a wrong answer, and was the round's only resolved regression. A CHECK needs at least one value-level reconciliation against a reference the agent did not compute itself.

## Criteria-value normalization (NEW cluster, opened by r1_contract's only regression)
- What didn't (confirmed by RESULT, `r1_contract`): 41978 regressed 1→0. It matched a filter criterion by the literal/type it assumed rather than the values actually present in the column (`int(y) == 2015` on the year column, while the workbook's own `=COUNTIF($G$14:$G$9696,"2015")` treats that column as TEXT). Seed and both control replicates used `str(y) == str(year)` plus `str(s).strip().lower() == 'open'` and scored 1.0. The agent even reasoned itself out of normalizing: "case-insensitive check usually safer, but instruction says 'open'".
- Promising but not yet tried: a rule to (a) print the DISTINCT values of any column you filter on before writing the comparison, (b) compare text criteria case- and whitespace-insensitively and numeric-looking criteria on both sides as strings, and (c) when the workbook contains its own equivalent computation (a formula, a summary column, a sample row), reproduce that number first and treat a disagreement as your bug. Note (c) already exists in prompt.md §3 as prose and was NOT exercised in 41978's trace — so the FORM (prose advice) is what failed, not the content; it needs to be a step in the CHECK recipe.

<!-- cap-evolve:insights-append-below -->

## Measurement: the screen's parent side goes stale (round 2)
- **What didn't (confirmed by RESULT, `r2_numeric`):** trusting `screen.py`'s Δ̄. It pairs the candidate against the parent's *stored* per-task rewards. In round 2 `parent_vs_gate_ref_drift` was **+0.0671** (r1_contract's stored 0.775 re-measured as 0.842), so the screen reported Δ̄ **+0.30** and `fixed: [38985, 41978, 49036]` on an edit whose true `gate_delta` was **0.0**. Use the screen ONLY as a kill filter; never let its Δ̄ or its `fixed` list shape the next round's design.
- **What worked:** `--gate-against control` on every round. A byte-identical replicate measured concurrently is the only trustworthy reference. Also: intersect the per-task diff against **both** control replicates — a task that "improved" against one control but passed in the other is unresolved, not fixed. Round 2's raw diff suggested 4 fixes; the both-controls intersection left exactly one (`49036`).

## Reading the workbook: the two-load `data_only` contract
- **What worked mechanically, but did not pay (RESULT, `r2_numeric`):** the token `data_only` appeared **0 times** in every r1_contract rollout; after the edit the agent does load both copies (visible in 33722's turn-2 block). So the rule was *exercised* — the form was right — yet `gate_delta` was 0.0. Keep it (it is a true property of openpyxl and cannot break a formula-free task), but do not expect further yield from restating it.
- **What worked (confirmed, the round's one genuine fix `49036`):** "**a format clause governs the digits; an inline example only shows the layout**". When the instruction states a rendering (`with .00 decimal`) and shows an example whose digits disagree (`e.g. 67% WIN RATE`), the clause wins and the example only fixes where the symbols and trailing words sit — gold was `66.67% WIN RATE`. The agent's failure mode was to call the instruction "ambiguous" and copy the example; naming that move as forbidden is what fixed it.

## Sentinel rules backfire: never tell the agent what an empty result "usually" becomes
- **What didn't (confirmed by RESULT, `r2_numeric`, regression `33722` 1.0→0.0):** the bullet "pre-filled `0`s tell you what an empty or unmatched source is supposed to become". The agent inverted it. Facing an empty subset in a range with NO pre-filled cells, it wrote: *"we should check if a pre-filled 0 was expected. Since there were no pre-filled values ... 0 is often used for empty results in these tasks"* — and filled `0`, specifically to satisfy the CHECK line "no target cell is unintentionally empty". Seed, parent and both controls scored 1.0 on this task.
- **Generalized rule:** a rule that explains what a sentinel MEANS hands the agent a sentinel to reach for. State the *forbidden move* (an unmatched lookup is a bug in the range or the match test; go find it) and never the *plausible value*. Note the interaction: adding a completeness check ("no cell unintentionally empty") without also forbidding filler creates pressure to fabricate one.
- **Adjacent, unmined, and the biggest remaining signal:** in **4 of the 7** r2 val failures the losing decision is introduced by hedge prose in the agent's own comments — `"Usually, in these types of 'dynamic' requests, it means"` (33722), `"This usually means if the value is like 0.1, 0.2"` (46646), `"usually implies lookup"` (5835), `"Fallback if O3 is empty, though the prompt says it's a dropdown"` (11842). The agent resolves an ambiguity by guessing and then never tests the guess against anything in the file. No round has yet targeted the *guess-without-a-test* move itself.
- **Also confirmed:** row-anchored windows. 33722's gold is `MEDIAN(FILTER(B{r}:$B$12, ...))` — the window shrinks by ROW, and dropping the first k *matches* instead coincides for the first few cells and then runs out of data. When each cell of a target column is "the same calculation, one row further down", the window must be anchored to that cell's own row.

## Not winnable from the prompt (stop spending rounds on these)
- **`341-40`** — the agent's written values matched gold exactly (its 7 changed Q cells are precisely gold's 7 diffs), but openpyxl's load→save rewrites `31133.024999999998` as `31133.025`, and the grader's `transform_value` `round(x, 2)` then yields 31133.03 vs gold's 31133.02. Confirmed at the sheet-XML level; explicitly re-assigning the exact float does not survive the round-trip. A float-repr artefact of the save path, not a capability.
- **`535-20`** — not reproducible locally: replaying the agent's exact approach gives the grader's `(True, '')` and matching non-empty counts (2578 vs 2578). Container openpyxl is 3.1.3, the local venv 3.1.5. Treat as environment variance.
- **`56427`** — dropped from round 2's pairing with `sandbox exec failed: 500 Server Error`. Infrastructure. If it reappears as a "regression", check the feedback string before believing it.

## The biggest single lever found in this run: tell the agent WHAT TO DO WHEN IT DOESN'T KNOW
- **What worked (confirmed by RESULT, `r3_decide`, ACCEPTED, 3 fixed / 0 broken vs both controls):** rounds 1–2 shipped facts about spreadsheets; round 2 came out flat. The accepted round shipped a *decision procedure* instead. The diagnosis that found it: in **4 of the 7** remaining failures the losing decision was introduced by the agent's own hedge prose — `"Usually, in these types of requests, it means"`, `"0 is often used for empty results in these tasks"`, `"usually implies lookup"`, `"Fallback if O3 is empty, though the prompt says it's a dropdown"`. Each settles a question about THE FILE using a belief about spreadsheets in general.
- **The procedure that fixed it** (prompt.md §4 DECIDE): quote the hedge phrases back as the symptom, then — (1) implement BOTH readings as functions of the cell address, do not argue about which is natural; (2) score each against a figure the file already fixes, in this preference order: a pre-filled cell inside `answer_position` → a cached formula result answering the same question → a total/summary already in the sheet → the parallel column; (3) print both scores and keep the reading that reproduces the file's number — **and if neither reproduces it, BOTH are wrong; do not pick the closer one, go print more cells.** That last clause matters: without it the agent picks the nearer guess and stops.
- **Grep for the tell.** Hedge tokens in the agent's own comments (`usually`, `probably`, `ambiguous`, `I'll assume`, `fallback`, `is often used`) are a cheap, high-precision predictor of a wrong answer in the same rollout. Cluster on them before clustering on feedback strings.

## Never state what a plausible value IS; state which move is forbidden
- **What didn't (confirmed, `r2_numeric`, regression 33722 1.0→0.0):** "pre-filled `0`s tell you what an empty or unmatched source is supposed to become". Facing an empty result in a range with NO pre-filled cells, the agent reasoned *"0 is often used for empty results in these tasks"* and wrote `0` — specifically to satisfy another of my own rules, "no target cell is unintentionally empty".
- **What worked (confirmed, `r3_decide`):** deleting that bullet and replacing it with scope language — "the pre-filled cells are a SAMPLE of the column you are asked to produce, so your rule has to keep running past them". 33722 recovered.
- **Generalized:** a rule that explains what a sentinel MEANS hands the agent a sentinel to reach for. Also audit new rules in PAIRS: a completeness requirement ("no cell unintentionally empty") added without simultaneously forbidding filler manufactures the exact failure it was meant to catch.

## The two mirror-image failures around one decision point
- `33722`: gold `=MEDIAN(FILTER(B{r}:$B$12,(C{r}:$C$12>0%)*(C{r}:$C$12<1%)))` — a **row-anchored shrinking window**. Computing one filtered list and then dropping its first *k* entries agrees for the first few cells and then silently runs out of data. **"The same calculation, one row further down" means the range is anchored to that cell's own row.**
- `5835`: gold `=SUMIFS(I:I,G:G,B{r},H:H,A{r})`, and its target range C3:C19 **does** hold pre-filled `0`s at C6:C9 — the sheet's own convention for an unmatched row, which gold extends to all 17 cells. The agent read the `0`s as "don't overwrite" and then answered its failing CHECK by adding `if val is not None:` three times, ending with 7 empty cells.
- **Both are the same decision resolved in opposite wrong directions**, which is why no fact fixed both and a procedure did. When a cluster contains two failures that are each other's mirror image, stop writing facts.

## A correction must change the rule, not the rule's scope — but scope ends at the DATA
- **What worked (confirmed, `r3_decide`, fixed 5835):** "a fix changes the RULE, not which cells the rule covers"; adding `if val is not None:` or restoring originals makes the check quieter while leaving the bug in place; and an untouched cell is still graded, as a claim that its original content was the expected answer.
- **What that rule costs if unbounded (caught on the SCREEN, `353-29`):** it over-fills. 353-29 wrote `179` cells where `178` were expected — `1 cell(s) hold a value where the expected output has none`. Gold row 90 is empty in init AND golden; A89 = 21 is the last data row. Fix: "**the scope ends where the DATA ends, not where `answer_position` ends**", plus a recipe that prints `max(keyed)` — the last row whose key column holds anything — before writing. With the bound added, 353-29 was clean on full val.
- **Reusable audit that made this catchable:** before spending a round, compute which currently-passing tasks depend on PRESERVING originals inside `answer_position` (gold == init for cells in range). Here 6 of 31: 13-1 (120 cells), 353-29 (116 non-blank), 55817 (21), 48588 (17), 379-36 (14), 52807 (12). Screen those alongside the targets — they are where a "write more" rule does its damage, and the screen localizes it cheaply.

## Calendar literals
- **Still live (NOT fixed by `r3_decide`; the rule was added and did not fire):** `46646` hardcodes February = 28 days while `B3 = 2016` sits in the sheet. Gold is `=B9/DAY(EOMONTH(1&B8&$B$3,0))` → 15/29 = 0.5172; the agent wrote 0.5357 (15/28). 10 of 12 cells differ. The general rule ("anything depending on a calendar depends on the year, and the year is in the sheet; use `calendar.monthrange(year, month)[1]`, never a literal 28/30/31/365") is present in both §4 and task_template step 2 as of `r3_decide` and still did not change the behaviour — so the next attempt needs a different FORM, not a restatement.
